# Headwater — a documentation governance system

> Headwater is an open-source command-line tool that checks a documentation tree on every commit: each document has a declared kind, each link between documents is checked, and each file is accounted for.

## Docs

- [Headwater changelog](https://headwater.tools/changelog/): Every tagged version of Headwater, newest first. An entry arrives when a tag is cut, and this page promises no interval between one tag and the next.
- [Headwater compared — LeanCTX, TrustGraph, Vale](https://headwater.tools/compare/): How Headwater differs from LeanCTX, TrustGraph and Vale: authors declare how documents relate, and no language model extracts it. With the arguments against Headwater.
- [Glossary — Headwater](https://headwater.tools/glossary/): Fifteen terms this site uses more than once, defined the way this site uses them. Not the full engine vocabulary — that lives in the specification.
- [How Headwater works](https://headwater.tools/how-it-works/): You declare the kinds of document you keep, authors link the documents, Headwater checks the result and generates the indexes. The four steps, and what Headwater does not check.
- [Headwater — a documentation governance system](https://headwater.tools/): Headwater is an open-source command-line tool that checks a documentation tree on every commit: each document has a declared kind, each link between documents is checked, and each file is accounted for.
- [Install — Headwater](https://headwater.tools/install/): Every way to install the headwater binary: a release download for Linux and macOS, an APT repository for Debian and Ubuntu, cargo, and a build from source.
- [The Headwater namespace — https://w3id.org/headwater/](https://headwater.tools/ns/): The permanent identifier that Headwater artifacts carry, what resolves under it, and why it is not the project domain.
- [Headwater's self-assessment](https://headwater.tools/proof/): Headwater checks its own documentation on every commit. The result of that check, what two experiments measured, and what nobody has measured yet.
- [Your first governed corpus](https://headwater.tools/tutorial/): Sixteen steps take an empty directory to a passing strict check, and you leave holding shelf, kind, facet, overlay and obligation.
